- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong reversal, model often overshoots early; cap forecast at 1–2 days above recent high.
- After a sharp spike in price, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment by 1–3 days unless sentiment confirms decline.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a 30-day spike, model often fails to adjust; apply 3–5 day lag correction in downward phase.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is bullish but price drops below 30-day moving average, model often ignores support; add 1–2 day lag to downward correction.
